papers.title: Protocol for telomere-to-telomere assembly of Borrelia genomes using a hybrid method.
papers.abstract: Borrelia has a linear chromosome and linear plasmids capped by hairpin telomeres that short-read sequencing cannot resolve. Here, we present a protocol for telomere-to-telomere assembly of Borrelia genomes. We describe steps for spanning B. burgdorferi culture, DNA extraction, and sequencing through hybrid genome assembly to generate complete Borrelia genomes. The pipeline integrates Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads to assemble hairpin telomeres, resolve paralogous linear and circular plasmids, and annotate and validate the assembled complete Borrelia genome. For complete de
papers.summary: This protocol describes a hybrid sequencing and assembly pipeline that combines Oxford Nanopore long reads with Illumina short reads to produce complete, telomere-to-telomere Borrelia genomes. It addresses the specific challenge of resolving the linear chromosome and linear plasmids capped by hairpin telomeres, which short-read sequencing alone cannot assemble. The workflow covers culture, DNA extraction, sequencing, assembly, plasmid resolution, and annotation/validation.

papers.title: MACS3: A Peak-calling Platform for Bulk and Single-cell Regulatory Genomics.
papers.abstract: Since the original publication of Model-based Analysis for ChIP-Seq (MACS), the software has been widely used to identify enriched genomic regions in ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, DNase-seq, and related regulatory genomics assays. Over the years, MACS has evolved substantially, with MACS version 3 (MACS3) now serving as the actively maintained implementation. MACS3 preserves the core MACS framework for fragment pileup, dynamic local background noise, statistical enrichment testing, and peak refinement, while adding functionality needed for contemporary bulk and single-cell workflows. It support
papers.summary: MACS3 is the actively maintained successor to the widely used MACS peak-calling software, preserving its core statistical framework for detecting enriched genomic regions while adding new capabilities for modern bulk and single-cell regulatory genomics assays. It supports a broader range of assays including ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, and DNase-seq, making it a versatile platform for peak detection across experimental modalities.

papers.title: Longitudinal characterization of mixed-genotype SARS-CoV-2 infections in a military cohort reveals compartmentalized viral populations.
papers.abstract: Mixed-genotype severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infections are a concern due to the potential generation of novel recombinants that give rise to new variants. To better understand intra-host viral dynamics, we analyzed specimens from 24 participants from the U.S. Military Health System's Epidemiology, Immunology, and Clinical Characteristics of Emerging Infectious Diseases with Pandemic Potential COVID-19 cohort with suspected mixed-genotype SARS-CoV-2 infections. From an initial 24 suspected cases, we confirmed 17 as genuine coinfections and graded them by evidence
papers.summary: This study tracked 24 military cohort participants with suspected mixed-genotype SARS-CoV-2 infections, confirming 17 as genuine coinfections and grading them by evidence strength. Longitudinal sampling revealed that distinct viral populations can occupy different anatomical compartments within the same host, suggesting compartmentalized viral dynamics that could influence recombination and variant emergence.

papers.title: Scalable assembly of Ascaris mitogenomes from whole-genome data reveals a novel clade.
papers.abstract: The genus Ascaris is an important group of giant parasitic roundworms, infecting over 700 million people globally and causing substantial economic losses in domestic pigs. Whilst species of Ascaris are morphologically indistinguishable, analysis of mitochondrial loci has revealed three clades (A, B, C) broadly associated with host species and geographic distribution. The diversity within these lineages may expand with the addition of further genomic data. Here, we present a bioinformatic framework for de novo assembly of complete mitochondrial genomes (mitogenomes) from low-coverage whole-geno
papers.summary: The authors developed a bioinformatic framework to assemble complete Ascaris mitochondrial genomes from low-coverage whole-genome sequencing data, enabling mitogenome recovery without dedicated mitochondrial enrichment. Applying this to existing datasets, they uncovered a novel clade within the genus, expanding the known mitochondrial diversity of these globally important parasites.

papers.title: Functional screening of ZIP8 naturally occurring variants identifies pathogenic mutations and trafficking defects.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of human genomic data has revealed a large number of naturally occurring variants, creating a major challenge for functional annotation. The human metal transporter SLC39A8 (ZIP8) is a clinically important divalent metal transporter, yet most of its documented variants remain uncharacterized. Here, we developed a workflow to functionally evaluate ZIP8 variants by integrating laser ablation inductively coupled plasma time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-TOF-MS) with scaled-up cell-based transport assays. Using this method, we systematically analyzed 33 naturally occurrin
papers.summary: The authors developed a functional screening workflow combining laser ablation ICP-TOF-MS with cell-based transport assays to characterize 33 naturally occurring variants of the metal transporter ZIP8 (SLC39A8). This approach identified pathogenic mutations and trafficking defects among previously uncharacterized variants, demonstrating a scalable method for functional annotation of genomic variants.

papers.title: Evaluating the pathogenic significance of unique chromosomal variants in craniosynostosis using patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells and mouse modelling.
papers.abstract: Unravelling causal links between unique structural/copy-number variants (SV/CNV) and associated phenotypes is essential for correct genetic counselling. We investigated two families in which patients with craniosynostosis had SV/CNV potentially dysregulating a fibroblast growth factor (FGF)-encoding gene; a 730 kb dup(4)(q21.21) including FGF5; and a complex 568 kb interspersed 13q12.11 duplication, located 841 kb from FGF9.
papers.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
papers.summary: This study investigates two families with craniosynostosis carrying structural or copy-number variants near FGF genes (a 730 kb duplication including FGF5 and a complex 568 kb duplication near FGF9). Using patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells and mouse models, the authors evaluate whether these unique variants are causally linked to the craniosynostosis phenotype, aiming to improve genetic counselling for such rare variants.

papers.title: Multi-variant GWAS and genomic prediction dissect the genetic architecture underlying tomato fruit weight.
papers.abstract: Tomato fruit weight is primarily controlled by stable genetic effects and domestication-/improvement-associated loci, including prominent chromosome 5 signals, and integrating SNP, INDEL, and SV diversity improves candidate-locus discovery, biological interpretation, and genomic prediction across environments. Tomato fruit weight (fw) is a major breeding target shaped by domestication, crop improvement, and environmental variation. We investigated the genetic architecture and genomic predictability of fw in the Varitome population representing the tomato domestication continuum, including Sola
papers.journal: TAG. Theoretical and applied genetics. Theoretische und angewandte Genetik
papers.summary: This study dissects the genetic architecture of tomato fruit weight using multi-variant GWAS that integrates SNPs, INDELs, and structural variants across the Varitome population, which spans the tomato domestication continuum. The authors identify stable genetic effects and domestication-/improvement-associated loci, notably on chromosome 5, and show that incorporating diverse variant types improves candidate-locus discovery, biological interpretation, and genomic prediction across environments.

papers.title: Large-scale benchmarking of prokaryotic annotation tools across thousands of species.
papers.abstract: Genome annotation is an important step in deriving functional meaning from prokaryotic sequencing data, yet systematic evaluations guiding tool selection are lacking. We present the first large-scale investigation of four prominent open-source annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes. This includes Escherichia coli strains for baseline performance, thousands of archaea and bacteria genomes, as well as frameshifted and metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.summary: This study benchmarks four widely used prokaryotic genome annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes, including E. coli, archaea, bacteria, and challenging inputs like frameshifted and metagenome-assembled genomes. It provides the first large-scale systematic comparison to guide tool selection for functional annotation of prokaryotic sequencing data.

papers.title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a genome-wide association meta-analysis and polygenic risk score.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a heritable trait with marked variability in expression and outcomes. Our aims were to discover new genetic loci associated with HCM and to test the effect of a new polygenic risk score (PRS) on incidence, phenotype and outcomes stratified by genotype status.
papers.summary: This study performs a genome-wide association meta-analysis to identify new genetic loci associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and develops a polygenic risk score (PRS). The PRS is then tested for its ability to predict HCM incidence, phenotype, and outcomes when stratified by genotype status. The findings aim to improve genetic risk prediction and understanding of HCM variability.

papers.title: Development of RS1-specific ACMG/AMP variant classification criteria with pilot variant curation.
papers.abstract: Gene-based therapies are being developed for retinal diseases, including RS1-related X-linked retinoschisis. Therefore it is essential to determine which variants are pathogenic and which are benign when enrolling patients. The Clinical Genome Resource (ClinGen) X-Linked Inherited Retinal Diseases (XLRD) Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) brings together clinician scientists, molecular biologists, and geneticists to apply their expertise and review the clinical, genetic, population, and functional evidence for variants. American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) guidelines have been modifie
papers.summary: This paper describes the development of gene-specific ACMG/AMP variant classification criteria for RS1, the gene underlying X-linked retinoschisis, by the ClinGen X-Linked Inherited Retinal Diseases Variant Curation Expert Panel. The authors adapted the general ACMG/AMP framework into RS1-specific rules and piloted them by curating actual variants, aiming to standardize pathogenicity calls ahead of gene therapy enrollment. This provides a practical, expert-vetted framework for classifying RS1 variants in clinical and research settings.

papers.title: Comparative performance of portable DNA extraction protocols and bioinformatics workflows for rapid detection of gram-negative bacteria and antimicrobial resistance using Oxford Nanopore sequencing.
papers.abstract: Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) enables rapid, portable pathogen identification and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) detection, but the reliability of downstream genomic analyses is highly dependent on DNA extraction quality, particularly in resource-limited settings. This study comparatively evaluated four portable bacterial DNA extraction protocols derived from three commercial kits to determine their impact on nanopore sequencing performance, bioinformatics workflow completion, and field deployability. Six gram-negative bacterial isolates (Escherichia coli, n = 4; Pseudomonas sp., n = 1; and
papers.summary: This study compares four portable DNA extraction protocols from three commercial kits for their impact on Oxford Nanopore sequencing-based detection of gram-negative bacteria and antimicrobial resistance genes. The authors evaluate how extraction quality affects sequencing performance, downstream bioinformatics workflow completion, and suitability for field deployment in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Biological Foundation Models for Complex Disease Research and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Complex diseases, including cancer, rare genetic disorders, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, arise from interactions among genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states that are difficult to capture using a single data type or biological scale. Biological foundation models address this challenge by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens and learning representations that can be transferred to downstream biomedical and clinical tasks. In this review, we examine two major model classes, genomic sequence foundation models and cell foundatio
papers.summary: This review surveys biological foundation models that treat nucleotides and genes as tokens, focusing on genomic sequence models and cell-based models for studying complex diseases. It argues these transferable representations can integrate multiple data types and biological scales to support clinical translation in cancer, rare disorders, and neuropsychiatric conditions.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Sequence Dataset of Rhodococcus qingshengii IEGM 267-Terpenoid Biotransformer Toward Genetic Functional Annotation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Microbial biotransformation of monoterpenoids is a promising approach for obtaining bioactive compounds. Rhodococcus species are attractive biocatalysts due to their metabolic versatility and ability to transform hydrophobic substrates. In this study, we investigated the catalytic potential of Rhodococcus qingshengii IEGM 267 toward carveol isomers and explored genomic features that may underlie this activity. Methods: The strain was cultivated in mineral medium supplemented with (-)-trans-carveol. Biotransformation products were analyzed by TLC and GC-MS. The draft geno
papers.summary: This study reports the draft whole-genome sequence of Rhodococcus qingshengii IEGM 267, a bacterium capable of biotransforming monoterpenoids like carveol. The genome provides a resource for identifying genes involved in terpenoid metabolism, potentially enabling genetic functional annotation of biocatalytic pathways.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of Listeria monocytogenes Isolated from Retail Yak Meat in Nyingchi, Xizang, China.
papers.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is a Gram-positive zoonotic pathogen responsible for listeriosis, a severe foodborne disease with high mortality in humans and animals. This study aimed to investigate the molecular epidemiology and genomic characteristics of L. monocytogenes isolated from raw yak meat in Nyingchi, Xizang, China. A total of 231 yak-related samples were collected in Nyingchi, consisting of 214 retail raw yak meat samples, 14 farm environmental samples, and 3 nearby water source samples. L. monocytogenes isolates were identified and characterized using culture-based methods, PCR serotyping
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study surveyed Listeria monocytogenes contamination in retail yak meat and related environmental samples from Nyingchi, Xizang, China, using culture-based isolation, PCR serotyping, and genomic characterization. It provides baseline data on the prevalence and molecular epidemiology of this foodborne pathogen in a region where such surveillance has been limited.

papers.title: A High-Resolution Stereo-Seq Spatial Transcriptomic Resource for Adult Holstein Cattle Liver.
papers.abstract: The bovine liver is a highly compartmentalized organ that plays essential roles in continuous gluconeogenesis and nitrogen recycling; however, its spatial molecular architecture has remained largely uncharacterized due to the limitations of traditional bulk and single-cell approaches. To address this gap, Spatial Enhanced Resolution Omics-sequencing (Stereo-seq) was utilized to generate a subcellular-resolution (500 nm) transcriptomic map of an adult Holstein cattle liver, and a refined reference-guided workflow was implemented to overcome standard annotation limitations in livestock. Raw sequ
papers.summary: This study generated a subcellular-resolution (500 nm) Stereo-seq spatial transcriptomic map of an adult Holstein cattle liver, providing the first detailed spatial molecular atlas of this highly compartmentalized organ. The authors developed a refined reference-guided workflow to overcome annotation limitations in livestock species, enabling spatially resolved characterization of hepatic zonation and metabolic functions.

papers.title: Unlocking cis-regulatory landscapes across 500 million years of evolution and disease mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Genomic DNA encodes regulatory information that determines where, when, and to what extent genes are expressed. Theoretically, we should be able to identify these transcriptional "instructions" by examining genomic DNA sequence alone, yet this has remained challenging. Here we present the Vertebrate Regulatory MOdule Detector (VRMOD), a method that accurately predicts gene regulatory sequences using only the query genomic sequences. We applied VRMOD to 309 Ensembl genomes, generating a compendium of high-resolution, genome-position-fixed cis-regulatory modules without parameter tuning. We perf
papers.summary: The authors present VRMOD, a method that predicts gene regulatory sequences (cis-regulatory modules) using only genomic DNA sequence, without requiring parameter tuning or species-specific training data. They applied it across 309 Ensembl vertebrate genomes spanning 500 million years of evolution, producing a large compendium of high-resolution regulatory annotations. This resource enables comparative regulatory genomics and helps link non-coding sequence to disease mechanisms.

papers.title: Phage bioinformatics tools: a review of computational approaches for bacteriophage research.
papers.abstract: Rising clinical interest in phage therapy and the exponential growth of metagenomic sequence catalogues have driven a rapid expansion of bacteriophage bioinformatics. More than 80 dedicated tools, mostly published since 2020, now span identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. Aimed at experienced practitioners and developers, this review synthesizes the field through the lens of three successive computational paradigms: sequence homology, bounded by database completeness; machine learning, constrained by labelled traini
papers.summary: This review surveys over 80 computational tools for bacteriophage research, most published since 2020, covering tasks such as phage identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. It organizes the field around three successive computational paradigms—sequence homology, machine learning, and emerging approaches—while highlighting the limitations imposed by database completeness and labelled training data.

papers.title: LAMBDA: a prophage detection benchmark for genomic language models.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based genomic sequence models represent an emerging frontier in computational biology. Yet, their embeddings have not yet shown the same level of predictive power as natural and protein language models, highlighting a gap between current implementations and theoretical promise. Existing benchmarks for DNA language models primarily focus on classifying regulatory elements in eukaryotic genomes, leaving open the fundamental question of whether these models learn sequence-level features across whole genomes. We introduce LAMBDA, a benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate genome langu
papers.summary: LAMBDA is a new benchmark for evaluating genomic language models on prophage detection, a task that requires learning sequence-level features across whole genomes. It addresses the gap left by existing benchmarks that focus mainly on eukaryotic regulatory elements, providing a rigorous test of whether DNA language models capture meaningful genomic signals.

papers.title: Identification of rare maternal copy number variants by genome-wide analysis of noninvasive prenatal screening data in 113,017 pregnant women.
papers.abstract: Knowledge of copy number variants (CNVs) is relevant to maternal and fetal health and can be obtained from noninvasive prenatal screening (NIPS) of pregnancy. However, genome-wide analysis of maternal CNVs using NIPS data has not been conducted in large populations.
papers.summary: This study analyzed genome-wide copy number variants (CNVs) in maternal DNA using noninvasive prenatal screening (NIPS) data from 113,017 pregnant women, identifying rare maternal CNVs at scale. It demonstrates that routine NIPS data can be repurposed for large-scale maternal CNV discovery, with potential relevance to maternal and fetal health.

papers.title: Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox: An Integrative Framework for Endpoint-Conditioned Evidentiary Sufficiency in Structure-to-Function Claims.
papers.abstract: Accurate coordinates for a represented protein state do not, by themselves, establish activity or any other condition-specific function. This article defines the Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox (DPSP) as the apparent conflict between structural accuracy and functional underdetermination and develops it as an integrative evidentiary assessment framework rather than a new theory or paradigm. The underlying problem has been longstanding, since structural genomics, function annotation, allostery, and disorder research each established that fold does not determine function and that function does
papers.summary: This article defines the 'Dynamic Protein Structure Paradox' (DPSP) as the gap between having accurate protein structure coordinates and being able to claim what function that protein performs. Rather than proposing a new theory, it offers an integrative framework for assessing whether structural evidence is sufficient to support structure-to-function claims, drawing on lessons from structural genomics, function annotation, allostery, and disorder research.

papers.title: Beyond Canonical Neoantigens: Emerging Technologies for Identification of Noncanonical Antigens and Implications for Personalized Cancer Vaccines.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, advances in sequencing technologies and computational pipelines enabled the development of personalized cancer vaccines (PCVs). Current PCV strategies primarily target cancer neoantigens generated by non-synonymous DNA mutations, which can result in altered amino acid sequences capable of eliciting tumor-specific immune responses. More recently, a distinct class of tumor-specific antigens (TSA), termed noncanonical or cryptic antigens, has emerged as an additional source of immunogenic targets. Unlike canonical neoantigens, noncanonical antigens typically cannot be identi
papers.summary: This review discusses emerging technologies for identifying noncanonical (cryptic) tumor-specific antigens, which arise from sources beyond standard DNA mutations such as alternative splicing, non-canonical translation, and post-translational modifications. It highlights how these cryptic antigens could expand the target repertoire for personalized cancer vaccines beyond conventional neoantigens.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Deciphering the Plant Cis-Regulatory Code.
papers.abstract: Much of the regulatory information that shapes plant gene expression lies outside protein-coding regions, including many loci associated with agronomic traits. Deep learning models use DNA sequences and multi-omics data to examine components of this cis-regulatory information. This review compares convolutional, Transformer-based and graph architectures used to represent local sequence features, chromatin state and three-dimensional genome organisation. We assess their applications to transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, non-coding variant prioritisation and
papers.summary: This review surveys deep learning architectures—convolutional, Transformer-based, and graph neural networks—that model plant cis-regulatory information from DNA sequence and multi-omics data. It compares how these models capture local sequence features, chromatin state, and 3D genome organization, and evaluates their use in predicting transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, and prioritizing non-coding variants. The paper is a methodological overview aimed at guiding plant genomics researchers in selecting and applying such models.

papers.title: Pangenomes aid accurate detection of large insertions and deletions from targeted sequencing: the case of cardiomyopathies.
papers.abstract: Gene panels represent a widely used strategy for genetic testing in a vast range of Mendelian disorders. While this approach aids reliable bioinformatic detection of short coding variants, it often fails to detect many larger variants. Recent studies have recommended the adoption of pangenome references (as opposed to linear reference genomes like GRCh38) to augment detection of large variants from targeted sequencing, potentially providing diagnostic laboratories with the possibility to streamline diagnostic work-ups and reduce costs.
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether using pangenome references instead of the standard linear reference genome (GRCh38) improves the detection of large insertions and deletions from targeted gene panel sequencing, using cardiomyopathies as a test case. The authors argue that pangenome-based analysis could help diagnostic laboratories detect larger variants that are currently missed, streamlining genetic testing and reducing costs.

papers.title: Expanding the Genomic Spectrum of NHLRC2-Associated FINCA Disease: Integrated Bioinformatic Characterization of a Novel Deep Intronic Variant Predicted to Activate a Pseudoexon.
papers.abstract: NHLRC2-associated FINCA disease is an ultra-rare autosomal recessive multisystem disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in NHLRC2. Its mutational spectrum and genotype-phenotype correlations remain incompletely defined, and the contribution of non-coding variants is poorly understood. Here, we report a male infant with a severe FINCA-like phenotype, including early-onset hemolytic anemia, pulmonary involvement, neurodevelopmental impairment, growth failure, recurrent infections, and fatal progression at 8.5 months. Whole-genome sequencing identified a compound heterozygous NHLRC2 gen
papers.summary: This case report describes a novel deep intronic variant in NHLRC2, identified via whole-genome sequencing in an infant with severe FINCA disease, that is predicted to activate a pseudoexon. The work expands the mutational spectrum of this ultra-rare disorder to include non-coding variants and integrates bioinformatic characterization to support pathogenicity.

papers.title: Potential Contribution of DES (p.Leu88Met) and MYH7 (p.Arg787His) Variants to Familial Restrictive Cardiomyopathy.
papers.abstract: Restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM) is a rare, severe cardiac disease with a heterogeneous genetic basis. Both genetic and nongenetic factors contribute to RCM pathogenesis. Identifying the underlying molecular causes is important for diagnosis and family screening. In this study, we investigated the genetic basis of RCM in a 52-year-old woman with a family history of RCM and heart disease.
papers.summary: This case study reports two rare genetic variants, DES p.Leu88Met and MYH7 p.Arg787His, in a 52-year-old woman with familial restrictive cardiomyopathy. The findings suggest these variants may contribute to the disease, highlighting the value of genetic testing for diagnosis and family screening in RCM.

papers.title: REAPER: a project-centric workflow layer for comparative repeatome analysis.
papers.abstract: Repeatome characterization from short-read sequencing data is widely performed using RepeatExplorer2/TAREAN. However, long-lived multisample projects and explicit comparative designs are often executed as ad hoc command sequences that are hard to version, rerun, and monitor on shared compute environments - a gap that motivates a project-centric workflow layer for repeatome analysis.
papers.summary: REAPER is a workflow layer built on top of RepeatExplorer2/TAREAN that organizes repeatome analysis around projects rather than ad hoc command sequences. It aims to make comparative repeatome studies easier to version, rerun, and monitor on shared compute environments.

papers.title: Short-read genome skimming enables molecular barcoding of old myxomycete collections.
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of Illumina-based genome skimming for barcoding myxomycete herbarium collections ranging from 29 to 91 years in age. We successfully retrieved partial sequences of the standard marker gene (nucSSU) in all cases, as well as additional markers (mtSSU, EF1a, and COI) for certain collections. Altogether, 28 genes were recognized in the studied material. In a 33-year-old specimen of Lindbladia tubulina, the assembly reached an N50 of 4.19 kb, enabling the recovery of extended functional loci. The input genomic DNA quantity emerges as the primary determinant of
papers.summary: This study shows that Illumina genome skimming can recover barcode and additional marker sequences from myxomycete herbarium specimens up to 91 years old, with the standard nucSSU marker retrieved in all samples. The amount of input genomic DNA was the main factor determining success, and one 33-year-old specimen yielded an assembly with an N50 of 4.19 kb. This demonstrates that old collections can be molecularly barcoded without fresh material.

papers.title: 'PePApipe': A complete bioinformatics analysis pipeline for African Swine Fever Virus genome.
papers.abstract: African Swine Fever Virus (ASFV) is of high concern in porcine livestock across the world due to both the high mortality rates and the trade restrictions imposed on affected regions. The viral genome is large and complex, and genomic analysis is essential for tracing its origin and evolution. Although several bioinformatics tools exist for genome assembly and analysis, no single platform integrates all necessary steps in an accessible and systematic way. In this study the authors developed 'PePApipe', a custom-built, user-friendly pipeline that enables rapid, complete, and efficient ASFV genom
papers.summary: The authors developed 'PePApipe', a user-friendly bioinformatics pipeline that integrates all necessary steps for African Swine Fever Virus genome assembly and analysis into a single platform. This addresses the lack of an accessible, systematic tool for analyzing the large and complex ASFV genome, which is critical for tracing viral origins and evolution.

papers.title: Correlation assessment of SARS-CoV-2 variants and their subvariants present in clinical and wastewater samples in Oregon, USA (February 7, 2021 - February 26, 2022) using the Freyja bioinformatics approach.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance is a valuable tool for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 at the community level. As the virus diversified into many variants and subvariants that share overlapping mutations, resolving them accurately from wastewater becomes a key bioinformatic challenge.
papers.summary: This study used the Freyja bioinformatics tool to analyze SARS-CoV-2 variants and subvariants in both clinical and wastewater samples from Oregon over roughly a year. It assessed how well wastewater-based variant tracking correlates with clinical surveillance data, addressing the challenge of distinguishing variants with overlapping mutations. The work supports wastewater surveillance as a reliable complement to clinical testing for community-level monitoring.

papers.title: Complete Genome Sequencing of Occult Hepatitis B Virus in Hemodialysis Patients Reveals Subgenotype D2 and Immune Escape Mutations in Bangladesh.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global health concern, and occult HBV infection (OBI) presents significant diagnostic and clinical challenges, particularly among hemodialysis (HD) patients. This study is aimed at characterizing complete HBV genomes from maintenance HD patients with OBI in Bangladesh to elucidate genetic features, mutational patterns, and clinical implications. Serum samples from two HBsAg-negative HD patients were screened by ELISA and quantitative PCR. Viral DNA was amplified by PCR across four overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) and sequenced on the Illumina platf
papers.summary: This study sequenced complete hepatitis B virus genomes from two hemodialysis patients in Bangladesh who had occult HBV infection (HBsAg-negative but viral DNA present). The viruses belonged to subgenotype D2 and carried mutations associated with immune escape, which may explain why standard antigen tests missed the infections. These findings highlight diagnostic and clinical challenges for monitoring HBV in dialysis patients.
